about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: a virtual exhibition at the intersection of video game and spatial research transports the viewer into a labyrinth built entirely from windows. the digital metaphor of infinity—the “window onto the world”—finally collapses, turning the promise of absolute open-world freedom into a claustrophobic trap where gameplay itself becomes a metaphor for subordination.
about.paragraph_2: there are no walls in the conventional sense: the labyrinth generates itself from an endless stream of windows. moving through this void, the player-viewer discovers that only the frames change: one urban grille gives way to another, one internet sign to the next. this is a simulator of total visual noise, where the landscape is infinite yet static in essence—interfaces change, but the horizon does not. within this gamified lack of freedom, however, lies a narrative rupture: escape from this space is still possible, elevating the project into a philosophical parable.
about.paragraph_3: moving through three-dimensional space, the player-viewer discovers that each window is a hybrid of an urban grille and internet signs. windows fill the horizon and turn from viewing tools into material for building walls. the portal has ceased to be an exit and become an obstacle.
about.paragraph_4: the monogram has historically been associated with luxury, power, and elitism. when a strict restriction—the grille—is disguised as elegant ornament, control ceases to be perceived as aggression.
about.paragraph_5: from this perspective, the viewer no longer looks through a window but at it, studying grilles, monograms, and pictograms as the only available landscape. the project gamifies control itself: the aesthetics of prohibition are presented as beautiful visual ornament, and navigation becomes a simulator of digital unfreedom.

exclamation.title: “!” sign
exclamation.text: a visualisation of a permanent state of emergency. the exclamation mark embedded in the grille turns the window from a viewpoint into a transmitter of commands—and then into a scream.

question.title: “?” sign
question.text: a codification of uncertainty. on the window grille, the sign legitimises and fixes the viewer’s disorientation as a permanent status. the space itself blocks every possibility of an answer.

sword.title: sword
sword.text: the disarming of the player: the sword as someone else’s weapon. in this labyrinth, the sword does not belong to the player. it is fused into the frame itself and blocks the view. the weapon that should traditionally be in the player’s hands has itself become a wall—a metaphor for powerlessness before the interface.

information.title: information
information.text: the trap of “excessive knowledge.” the player sees the information icon and moves closer to read the context—to find a clue for navigating the labyrinth—but that very step and faith in the offered narrative lead to a dead end. information here is not the key to escape.
